observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x0045b216 MOV dword ptr [EBP-0x60],ECX spills ECX and 0x0045b221 MOV ECX,dword ptr [EBP-0x60] reloads it, so ECX is the receiver. EDX is never read by the body, which rules out __fastcall. 0x0045b286 RET 0x4 rules out cdecl. Ghidra's decompilation mislabels the single register parameter as __fastcall because the incoming stack word is passed onward by address, but the machine shape is unambiguously __thiscall plus one callee-cleaned stack word.

observed_mechanics: 0x0045b213: SUB ESP,0x60 allocates 96 bytes for what the body actually uses as six 4-byte slots
0x0045b219: LEA EAX,[EBP + 0x8] takes the ADDRESS of the incoming stack word; 0x0045b21c PUSH EAX passes it onward
0x0045b21d / 0x0045b220: LEA ECX,[EBP-8] then PUSH ECX makes the callee's first stack argument the out-pair address, so the callee signature is (&out_pair, &id_word)
0x0045b224: ADD ECX,0x8 makes the embedded map, which lives at receiver+0x8, the callee's receiver
0x0045b227: CALL 0x00421950 is the only call in the body
0x0045b238: MOV ECX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x8] reads the bucket count at map+0x8, i.e. receiver+0x10
0x0045b23e: MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX + 0x4] reads the bucket array base at map+0x4, i.e. receiver+0xc
0x0045b241: LEA ECX,[EAX + ECX*0x4] forms buckets[bucket_count], one past the end of the bucket array: the end sentinel slot
0x0045b24a: MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX] dereferences that sentinel slot, so the value compared against is the sentinel NODE pointer
0x0045b25b: MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP-8] takes the callee's first output word, the entry pointer
0x0045b25e / 0x0045b260 / 0x0045b263: XOR ECX,ECX then CMP then SETZ CL is the compiler lowering of an equality test into a byte
0x0045b269: TEST EDX,EDX with 0x0045b26b: JZ 0x0045b271 means EQUALITY takes the branch to the value load, so a match with the sentinel is the zero-return path
0x0045b26d: XOR EAX,EAX produces the dword 0 on the sentinel-match path
0x0045b27a: MOV EDX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x4] reads node+0x4, the mapped value, on the mismatch path

control_flow.branch_polarity: The polarity is the opposite of the naive reading and is the single most important detail of this function. SETZ CL at 0x0045b263 materialises the equality, JZ at 0x0045b26b then takes the branch WHEN EQUAL. Equality with the sentinel is the not-found shape produced by the callee at 0x00421a11..0x00421a0e, so EQUALITY must yield 0, and the fallthrough MISS must yield the value. XOR EAX,EAX at 0x0045b26d sits on the fallthrough, confirming that the fallthrough is the zero path.

callees_evidence.name: FUN_00421950
callees_evidence.shape: __thiscall with two callee-cleaned stack words (RET 0x8 at 0x00421a3f), 86 instructions, body read in full
callees_evidence.operation: Chained hash-map lookup. Receiver = this+0x8 of the caller. Stack arguments are (&out_pair, &id_word) in that order. Computes bucket = buckets[id % bucket_count], loads the chain head from buckets[bucket_index], walks node+0x8 while node+0 != id, and writes the two-word out pair. On a hit the pair is {node, &buckets[bucket_index]} (0x004219d1..0x004219da). On a miss, at 0x004219e5..0x00421a0e, the pair is {*end, end} where end = buckets + bucket_count*4. The 0x00421a28..0x00421a36 stores copy both words out through the caller's pointer and 0x00421a3c..0x00421a3f return that pointer.
callees_evidence.naming_basis: The decompilation, the full instruction listing and the two call sites all agree, and the structure is a textbook chained hash map with a key at node+0, a value at node+0x4 and a next pointer at node+0x8. No SDK name is asserted for it.

callees_evidence.name: FUN_00401050
callees_evidence.form: CALL at every one of the sampled call sites, immediately before this function
callees_evidence.shape: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / MOV EAX,dword ptr [0x015d0c14] / POP EBP / RET -- five instructions, bare RET
callees_evidence.operation: Global registry pointer accessor. Its whole role at these sites is to materialise the `this` for this function while leaving the caller's pushed id word on the stack, which its bare RET guarantees. It is not a real callee of this function; it is an accessor the compiler inlined at the call site and the decompiler attributes to the same basic block.

sibling_and_analogue_functions.observation: Same map, same end-sentinel idiom. On a hit it returns node+4, the ADDRESS of the value slot; on a miss it creates the entry through 0x0045b4c0 and then also returns node+4. The difference in return shape between this function (the value) and 0x0045b290 (the slot address) is what pins this function as a value getter.
Unlinks a node from a chain, calls 0x0045b6f0 on it, decrements the count at map+0xc and returns the successor pair. Its body confirms the chain-walk and the {next, slot} pair shape.

Walks every entry of the same map, calls vtable slot +0x0c with argument 1 on each mapped object, then frees the bucket array and clears map+0xc. This proves the mapped values are polymorphic objects with a live vtable, which is why every caller dispatches on the return value.

Creates an object through a factory reached at vtable slot +0x2c, and when param_3 == 1 replaces the map entry for the id through 0x0045b290. This is the write path that populates the map this function reads, and it is why a miss is a normal state rather than an error.

sdk_candidates.observation: A grep of ~/apps/Spore-ModAPI/Spore for registry- or FindById-shaped declarations returned nothing, and Spore/Editors/Editor.h was read in full without a matching member. The shape is a hand-rolled chained hash map rather than an exposed SDK container, so no container type and no method name is claimed.
sdk_candidates.not_asserted: The registry class, the container type, the meaning of the 32-bit id space, and the interface behind the six observed virtual slots are all NOT claimed.

semantic_contract: Given a receiver R holding a chained hash map at R+0x8 and a 32-bit id, the function returns the mapped dword stored at node+0x4 of the entry whose node+0 equals the id, and returns the literal dword 0 when no such entry exists. Absence is detected by comparing the lookup result against the map's end sentinel, which is the dword one slot past the end of the bucket array, buckets[bucket_count]; that is the same end() idiom the map's own lookup uses rather than an added guard, and both this function and the callee compute that address independently. The function is a pure read: it writes no receiver or map byte, has no side effects, and mutates nothing. A mapped value of 0 is indistinguishable from absence, so the only usable caller contract is 'non-zero means an object was found'; every sampled caller uses it exactly that way. In every sampled use the mapped value is an object pointer whose vtable is then dispatched at slot +0x00, +0x08, +0x0c, +0x18, +0x2c or +0x30 with the returned pointer as the receiver. The id is passed to the callee by address rather than by value, so the function performs no direct load of its own stack argument; that indirection is invisible in the decompiled pseudocode but is what the reconstruction reproduces.
classification_rationale: Every instruction of the body and of its single callee 0x00421950 was read directly, including the node layout, the bucket arithmetic, the end-sentinel construction, the chain walk and the miss/hit polarity, and eleven call sites corroborate the return contract including six distinct virtual dispatches on the returned value. Two material elements stay bounded. First, the owning type of the registry: its only proven address is the global pointer slot 0x015d0c14, no vtable was located for the object it points at, and the binary has no RTTI, so the registry class is unnamed. Second, the meaning of the 32-bit id space: two sampled ids are hardcoded constants with the shape of hashed type ids, but no hashing routine was located and the SDK exposes no matching enumeration, so 'type id' remains a candidate rather than an established fact. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld because the reconstructed behaviour is not fully determined without naming what the ids are and who owns the map; STRUCTURAL_ONLY would understate the evidence, since the behavioural contract and the callee's operation are both established rather than merely the layout.
semantic_findings: The function is a value-returning map lookup, not a handle and not an index. The distinction is pinned at instruction level by 0x0045b27a, which dereferences the node, versus the sibling 0x0045b290, which returns node+4 without dereferencing.
Absence is signalled by 0, and because 0 is also a legal stored value the observable contract is only 'non-zero means found'. Every sampled caller branches on exactly that.

The end sentinel is buckets[bucket_count], one past the last bucket. Both this function and the callee compute that address independently, which is the classic signature of a hash_map end() iterator rather than a null terminator.

The branch polarity is inverted relative to the naive reading: SETZ CL at 0x0045b263 followed by JZ at 0x0045b26b means the branch is taken ON equality, and equality is the not-found shape, so the branch target is the value load and the fallthrough carries XOR EAX,EAX. Reading this as 'equal means found' would invert the function's entire contract.

The receiver in every sampled call site is the value of the global pointer at 0x015d0c14, read through the 0x00401050 accessor thunk whose bare RET is what preserves the pushed id. That global is zero in the static image, so the registry is populated entirely at runtime.

The key space is a set of hardcoded 32-bit constants: 0xb8deeb8b at 0x0058bf39 and 0xabf6fbdd at 0x0043f951 are both pushed literally into the same registry, and cEditor carries a runtime id at +0x27c and another at +0x278.

The mapped values are polymorphic objects. 0x0045afc0 dispatches slot +0x08, 0x0045b000 slot +0x0c, 0x0045b040 slot +0x18, 0x0045b110 slot +0x30 and cEditor::Update slots +0x00 and +0x2c, all with ECX equal to the returned value.

The map is populated through 0x0045ac20, which creates an object via a factory at vtable slot +0x2c and then installs it with the paired setter 0x0045b290. A miss is therefore an expected state, not an error path.

The incoming stack word is read only by address. 0x0045b219 takes LEA EAX,[EBP+8] and 0x0045b21c pushes it; the body itself never executes a load from EBP+8. This is why the Ghidra decompilation shows a fictitious 'stack0x00000004' argument and why the reconstruction passes &id to the port.
unresolved_questions: What class owns the map? The only proven address is the global slot 0x015d0c14 and no vtable was located for the registry object, so the owning type is unnamed.
What does the 32-bit id denote? Two sampled values look like hashed type ids, but no hashing routine was located and the SDK exposes no matching enumeration, so 'type id' stays a candidate.

Which code writes a non-zero value into the global at 0x015d0c14? Only the clearing write at 0x005d61e7 was located; the populating write is not in the observed xref set, so it may be an indirect or registration-time store.
What are the concrete classes behind the mapped objects? Six virtual slots are observed across five call sites but no vtable base was resolved, so the interface is unnamed.
Can a mapped value legitimately equal 0? If so, that entry is permanently invisible to every caller. Nothing in the static evidence answers this.
Are 0x0045afc0 / 0x0045b000 / 0x0045b040 / 0x0045b110 thin wrappers over a named SDK method or a hand-rolled dispatch table? The body shape is a bare guarded virtual call, which fits either.
Is the bucket count fixed or rehashed at runtime? 0x0045b4c0 (the miss-path inserter reached from 0x0045b290) was not read, so rehash behaviour is unestablished.
Fourteen of the twenty-five reported call sites were not disassembled window-by-window in this batch; their receiver provenances come from the briefing's call graph.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists, so the claim that the global at 0x015d0c14 is populated and that lookups succeed is static only.
A runtime pass would need to record the bucket count and the resolved object pointer for a handful of the hardcoded ids to confirm the id-to-class mapping.
The original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run, so no stage-level reachability claim is made.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 45-instruction body is reconstructed in full as machine-observable semantics, including the by-address forwarding of the id and the end-sentinel comparison. The map body layout is declared only to the extent the two instructions that touch it require.
preserved_semantics: the id reaches the callee by address, not by value
the map lives at receiver+0x8 and the callee's receiver is that address
the compared sentinel is buckets[bucket_count], one past the last bucket
equality with the sentinel returns the dword 0, and any other result returns node+0x4
nothing in the receiver or the map is written
the stack word is callee-cleaned (RET 0x4), modelled with __attribute__((thiscall))
body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: not claimed. clang++ 22.1.8 -m32 -O2 emits a stack-protector-instrumented 0x84-byte form with a canary load and store, against the original's 121 bytes with a 0x60-byte frame. The observable behaviour, the return value, the return width and the callee-cleaned epilogue match; the frame, the spill slots and the encoding do not.

validation.model_test_coverage: a miss returns 0 and performs exactly one lookup; a hit returns node->value; the forwarded key is captured by value and compared against the requested id; a stored value of 0 is shown to be indistinguishable from a miss
